caption:
Comment BLUEPRINT and I'll send it over: the whole faceless model, written out.

"Isn't this just a pyramid scheme?" Fair question. Here's the actual answer.

THE REAL DIFFERENCE

A pyramid scheme pays you when people below you recruit more people. There's no real product, just money moving upward until it collapses.

Affiliate marketing pays you when someone buys something real. No one signs up under you. No downline, no levels, nobody you have to recruit to make this work.

HOW THE MONEY ACTUALLY MOVES

You post about a product. Someone clicks and buys it, a real purchase, not a signup fee. The company pays you a commission, once. That's the whole chain. Nobody signs up under you, ever.

THE 10-SECOND TEST

Ask one question about any offer, this one included. Would it exist without new recruits paying to join? If the answer is no, that's the scheme. If the answer is yes, that's just business.

WHY THIS MATTERS

A pyramid scheme burns trust to make one fast round of money before it collapses. This only works if people keep buying from the same recommendation, over and over. Burn trust once, and the recurring income stops recurring.

THE HONEST PART

I'm not going to tell you what you'll make. I don't know you, and I don't know how hard you'll work. Anyone who quotes you a number they can't back is selling you a feeling.

It could be zero. If you post twice and quit, it's zero. This is not easy and it's not passive on day one.

But it is simple, and nobody has to sign up under you for any of it to work.

Comment BLUEPRINT and I'll send it over.
